data.name: Hariz
data.gender_notes: Hariz is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'hara'a, meaning 'to cultivate or till land'. A name for a righteous and hardworking man. The name Hariz carries the meaning “Gardener” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Hariz usually hope their child will grow to embody gardener and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing growth, nurturing, and the cultivation of good deeds.
data.etymology: Hariz belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gardener.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hariz total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_urdu.name: حارز

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Hariz ibn Umayya al-Asadi: A prominent poet and companion of Caliph Harun al-Rashid. The name Hariz carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Hariz was born into a noble Arab family in Iraq around 760 AD. He is best known for his poetic compositions in Arabic, particularly his quasida poems, which were dedicated to various caliphs and their courts. Hariz's poems often touched on themes of love, nature, and the passage of time. He was a close companion of Caliph Harun al-Rashid, who ruled the Islamic empire from 786 to 809 AD. Hariz's poetry was celebrated during the caliph's court and he was a regular participant in poetic gatherings and contests. Hariz died around 830 AD.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Hariz al-Balkhi: A Persian scholar, astronomer, and mathematician. The name Hariz carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Hariz al-Balkhi, also known as Al-Biruni, was born in Khwarezmia (present-day Uzbekistan) around 973 AD. He is considered one of the greatest scholars of the Islamic Golden Age. Hariz made significant contributions to various fields, including astronomy, mathematics, geography, and philosophy. He wrote numerous works on these subjects, many of which were groundbreaking and influential. Hariz's most famous work is 'Al-Qanun al-Masihi', a comprehensive astronomical treatise that covers a wide range of astronomical topics and includes tables for predicting eclipses and planetary positions. Hariz died around 1048 AD in India, where he had been invited by the emperor to serve as a scholar and advisor.
